newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIAN HARD CURRENCY LOANS 8.3 PCT UP IN JULY.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIAN HARD CURRENCY LOANS 8.3 PCT UP IN JULY.

text.p: Hard currency loans in Romania continued a recent upswing in July when they were 8.3 percent up from June, the National Bank (BNR) said.
Hard currency credits took 33.6 percent of total end-July non-government credits, which stood at 21.01 trillion lei 5.7 percent up from the previous month, a BNR report said.
It said the central bank had issued in July rules on commercial banks' foreign exchange liquidity to improve their position and discourage hard currency loans.
Loans in the local leu currency -- mostly short-term ones -- expanded by 4.4 percent to 13.95 trillion lei at end-July.
Commercial banks' average leu lending rate for non-bank customers eased to an annual 56.8 percent in July from 57.4 percent in June.
State companies held 57.7 percent of end-July leu loans, down from 58.9 percent in June.
Inflation was 7.5 percent in July, with the year-on-year rate was 40.3 percent. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
